title: Sensory Learning and Exploration
summary: Gentle ways to explore touch, movement, sensory environments and personal choices.

chapters.title: Touch and texture
chapters.summary: Explore safe textures at the child's pace.

subchapters.title: Touch and texture
subchapters.body:
Offer two safe objects with different textures. Let your child touch, look at, smell or avoid them. There is no need to force touching. Watch for signals that say more, stop or change.

**A break is a valid response.**
subchapters.takeaway: Sensory exploration should be safe and voluntary.

questions.q: What should an adult do when a child does not want to touch an object?
options: Offer a break or another way to explore
Hold the child's hand onto it
Keep asking until they touch it
questions.explanation: Children communicate preferences through actions and signals. Exploration should remain voluntary.

quiz.q: Which is a good sensory practice?
quiz.explanation: Following signals supports safety and trust.

quiz.q: Can looking at an object be a form of exploration?
quiz.explanation: Children can explore with different senses and do not have to touch everything.

quiz.q: What can a break communicate?
options: The child needs a pause or change
quiz.explanation: A break is useful communication.

quiz.q: How many objects should you start with?
quiz.explanation: A small number reduces overload.

quiz.q: Should texture activities be forced?
quiz.explanation: Sensory learning should be safe and voluntary.

chapters.title: Pour and scoop
chapters.summary: Build fine-motor practice through predictable play.

subchapters.title: Pour and scoop
subchapters.body: Use a tray, cup and spoon with water or a dry material. Demonstrate scoop, carry and pour. Start with a small amount and allow your child to watch or copy. Keep the activity supervised.
subchapters.takeaway: Repeated, predictable actions can support learning.

options: It defines a manageable play space
questions.explanation: A tray gives the activity a clear boundary, although some mess is expected.

quiz.q: What is a helpful first step?
quiz.explanation: A slow demonstration makes the sequence predictable.

quiz.q: Should water play be supervised?
quiz.explanation: Children should be supervised around water and small materials.

quiz.q: What can a child do instead of pouring?
quiz.explanation: Participation can take different forms.

quiz.q: What supports predictability?
quiz.explanation: A repeated sequence is easier to anticipate.

quiz.q: What should an adult accept?
quiz.explanation: Attempts and pauses provide useful information.

chapters.title: Move and play
chapters.summary: Use safe movement and follow the child's lead.

subchapters.title: Move and play
subchapters.body: Offer one movement at a time: stretch, push, roll or jump. Demonstrate, pause and let your child choose whether to join. Keep the space clear and stop when movement no longer feels comfortable.
subchapters.takeaway: Movement is most useful when it feels safe and enjoyable.

questions.q: What should happen after demonstrating a movement?
options: Pause and give the child time
questions.explanation: A pause gives the child time to process and respond.

quiz.q: How many new movements should you introduce first?
quiz.explanation: One movement is easier to understand.

quiz.q: Should movement be forced?
quiz.explanation: The child should be able to pause or decline.

quiz.q: What makes movement safer?
quiz.explanation: A clear space reduces hazards.

quiz.q: What should adults notice?
quiz.explanation: Comfort and communication matter more than performance.

quiz.q: Can watching count as participation?
quiz.explanation: Watching can be an important first step.

chapters.title: Sensory walk
chapters.summary: Notice one feature of a familiar environment.

subchapters.title: Sensory walk
subchapters.body: Take a short familiar walk and notice one sound, color, texture or movement. Keep the route predictable. Offer headphones, a quiet route or a return home when needed.
subchapters.takeaway: Noticing can be gentle and selective.

questions.q: What is a good sensory-walk goal?
questions.explanation: One feature keeps the task manageable.

quiz.q: What route is best to begin with?
quiz.explanation: Familiarity can reduce uncertainty.

quiz.q: What can help with sound?
quiz.explanation: Environmental adjustments can support comfort.

quiz.q: How many features should you notice first?
quiz.explanation: One focus is easier to manage.

quiz.q: Can a child choose to return home?
quiz.explanation: A return or break is a valid choice.

quiz.q: What matters more than finishing?
quiz.explanation: Safety and comfort guide the activity.

subchapters.title: Sort by shape
subchapters.body: Start with two groups of safe objects. Show the sorting rule, such as round and not round, then let your child place objects. Add a third group only when the first rule is comfortable.
subchapters.takeaway: One clear rule makes sorting easier.

questions.explanation: A single rule reduces the thinking load.

quiz.q: How many groups are a good starting point?
quiz.explanation: Two groups are easier to compare.

quiz.q: What is a sorting rule?
options: A feature used to group items
quiz.explanation: Shape or color can be a sorting feature.

quiz.q: When should you add another group?
options: When the first rule is comfortable
quiz.explanation: Increase complexity gradually.

quiz.q: Can the child point instead of speak?
quiz.explanation: Communication can be spoken, gestural or visual.

quiz.q: What should adults praise?
quiz.explanation: Effort and engagement support learning.

chapters.title: My sensory choices
chapters.summary: Support communication about comfort and preferences.

subchapters.title: My sensory choices
subchapters.body: Offer two safe options, such as quiet or music, soft or rough, and ask your child to point, gesture, speak or use a picture. Honour the answer and offer a break when requested.
subchapters.takeaway: A choice or a break is communication.

questions.q: What should happen after a child makes a sensory choice?
questions.explanation: Honouring choices teaches that communication works.

quiz.q: How many options should you offer first?
quiz.explanation: Two options are easier to compare.

quiz.q: Can a picture communicate a choice?
quiz.explanation: Pictures are valid communication.

quiz.q: What does a break request communicate?
quiz.explanation: A break is useful information about comfort.

quiz.q: Should safe choices be honoured?
quiz.explanation: Respecting choices builds trust and self-advocacy.

quiz.q: What is the goal?
quiz.explanation: The goal is communication and supported participation.
